To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have designed and prototyped a Resonant Switch Capacitor DCDC converter for a power distribution system in a harsh environment.
the design of a Resonant Switching DCDC converter, based on an ASIC, for the LHC upgrade has been carried out.

the Resonant Switch Capacitor converter can be optimized for a better performance in terms of efficiency, mass and volume, and the design of a new version of the converter is possible, with a higher efficiency and reliability, and a better control of the output voltage.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new generation of DCDC converter, that will be used to supply the analog and digital circuits of the detectors of the High Luminosity upgrade of the LHC experiments.
the optimization of the efficiency and the design of the analog circuits of a DCDC converter, that will be used for the High Luminosity upgrade of the LHC experiments at CERN.
the design of analog circuits that can be used in a resonant Switched Capacitors converter, and the design and optimization of this converter itself.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this project has been successfully concluded, and the results obtained have been very satisfactory.
, thanks to the improvements carried out, the converter is able to reach a peak efficiency up to 94% and an output current up to 2A, with a total mass of 2.4g and an overall size of 3.6cm2.
the work carried out in this project has led to a better understanding of the converter operation and to an improvement of its efficiency, reliability and performances.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the converter efficiency has been increased up to 96%, the output voltage ripple has been reduced, the output voltage has been made less sensitive to temperature changes, and the converter reliability has been improved.
we have been able to increase the maximum efficiency of the converter by 2% and we have been able improve the converter reliability.
the design of the converter has evolved from a prototype to a fully functional circuit.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the efficiency optimization and the redesign of the analog blocks allowed us to increase the efficiency of the resonant DCDC by 2% and to reduce the mass by 30%, with respect to the previous prototype.

, thanks to the optimization performed, the resonant switched capacitor converter is now ready for the next phase of the project, that is the integration in a multi chip module (MCM) together with other converters, and the final test in the harsh environment of the LHC.

a resonant switched capacitor converter is a viable solution for the last step in a DCDC converter chain, and that the converter efficiency can be improved by carefully designing the control circuitry.
